The main takeaway from our work is that

the sizing of cryogenic refrigeration plants for large-scale projects can be based on estimates of the static heat loads, provided that adequate overcapacity is added for the dynamic loads, whose magnitude is not predictable a priori, and that adequate margins are left to cope with the uncertainty on heat loads.

, in the case of complex machines with large number of components, a conservative approach to the sizing of the cryogenic system can be adopted, provided that a thorough and systematic R&D program is conducted, that the heat load estimates are based on sound physics and engineering, and that a proper margin is included.

the design of the cryogenic system for the LHC was based on the best knowledge of the time and on the best available technology, but it was also based on the understanding that the system would need to be operated in a dynamic mode, with excess refrigeration capacity to absorb the dynamic loads.
